title: API 650 welded atmospheric storage tanks: one-foot method shell thickness, allowable stresses, minimum thickness
note: API Std 650 is paywalled; formulas and table rows below are public extracts cross-checked between independent sources. Clause numbers differ between editions (3.6.x in old editions, 5.6.x since the 11th edition).

SI.units: D nominal tank diameter m, H design liquid level above the bottom of the course m, G design specific gravity, Sd / St allowable product-design / hydrostatic-test stress MPa, CA mm

USC.units: D ft, H ft, S psi, CA in

oneFootMethod.governing: t = max(td, tt), not less than the minimum nominal thickness for the tank diameter, rounded up to a commercial plate
oneFootMethod.applicability: not for tanks larger than 60 m (200 ft) in diameter (variable-design-point method instead)
oneFootMethod.gradeReason: same SI and USC forms in >= 3 independent extracts (epcland, midstreamcalculator, industrialmonitordirect, PPNS journal); some sheets divide by a joint efficiency E (Appendix A tanks)

published.governing: minimum thickness (6 mm stated by the article)

workedExample.gradeReason: one extract; values re-derived exactly from the grade-A formula, and Sd/St = 137/154 MPa agree with the A283 Gr C row of the stress table below

allowableStressRows.remark: one software printout shows 174.4 / 196.5 MPa (unrounded); not used

stressBasis.text: Sd <= 2/3 yield and <= 2/5 tensile; St <= 3/4 yield and <= 3/7 tensile (public summaries)

minimumNominalThickness.conflict: one extract says 6 mm for the lowest course when 3.2 m < D < 15 m, the PPNS example also applies 6 mm at D = 7.7 m; edition-dependent. llull ships this table as data with its edition, flags rows below grade A as unverified and never uses them silently (EQP_TABLE_UNVERIFIED warning).
